summary: I built the `--report <file>` seam as designed. App.xaml.cs parses report mode strictly, deletes any stale report first, and uses exit codes 0, 2, 3 and 70. MainWindow gains only an internal EndingShown event and a LastResult property, with no rendering line changed. WindowReport.cs reads the controls' Text after Dispatcher.Yield(Loaded) and writes schema-1 JSON in pure ASCII through a .tmp file and a move. eng/read-window.ps1 quotes the arguments, bounds the wait and prints EXIT plus the JSON, or NO REPORT. The obligations needed engine-runnable tests, so I added tests/window/WindowCases.ps1. Each of its 12 cases builds a tree in %TEMP%, runs the published single-file exe (publishing it first if it is stale) and checks the window's text against the tree it built. All 12 pass one by one, the build has 0 warnings and the 86 Core tests pass.

files.why: Adds --report: strict parsing (no value, no root or an extra argument gives exit 2); GetFullPath, then delete-first of <file> and <file>.tmp, with a missing parent folder or a directory path giving exit 3 before any window; a DispatcherUnhandledException handler (Discard, then Shutdown(70)); and an EndingShown handler where only the first ending counts, followed by WindowReport and Shutdown(0), or 3 on an IO failure. The launch without --report is unchanged.

Adds the internal EndingShown event, raised as the last statement of ShowOutcome and ShowProblem, and internal LastResult, set at the top of ShowOutcome and cleared beside `_result = null` in StartScan. Only lines were added; no formatting, layout or wording line moved.

Reads OutcomeTitle, OutcomeDetail, CountersText and OutcomePanel (IsVisible, ActualHeight) after Dispatcher.Yield(Loaded). Raw ScanResult numbers go only into `core`. It serialises with System.Text.Json's default encoder, so the file is ASCII with no BOM, writes .tmp and then File.Move(overwrite). The header documents the command line, the exit codes, the schema and the add-never-rename rule.

The thin reader from the design: a fresh GUID report path under %TEMP%\fsa-window, quoted arguments with trailing backslashes doubled, Start-Process -PassThru with the handle cached, WaitForExit(timeout) and a kill of its own process on timeout. It prints EXIT n or TIMEOUT, then the JSON or NO REPORT, and asserts nothing.

The tests the case obligations need: -Case C-001 to C-014 (or All). They publish through eng/dotnet.ps1 when the exe is missing or older than any source, build the case's tree in %TEMP%, run the exe through the reader (or through Start-Process directly for the raw-argument cases), check the window text against the tree built, clean up, and exit 0 or 1.

obligations.how: Owed to validate-slice; I cannot discharge it. Evidence toward it: `git diff` of MainWindow.xaml.cs shows only added lines (the event, LastResult, one reset and two raises), with no formatting, layout or wording line moved in ShowOutcome or ShowProblem. Architecture rule 2's three patterns match 0 times, even with comments included. Case C-011 shows a launch without --report is still open 5 s after launch, when its ending came within 0.9 s in report mode, and writes no file.

Owed to validate-slice. Evidence toward it: in this build node, engine-spawned and unelevated, every window case rendered the real window. OutcomePanel.visible was true and actualHeight was 369 or 423 in every report. The validate node itself has not run yet.

WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-001: 20 files of 64 KiB multiples in 4 folders, read through eng/read-window.ps1. Checks exit 0, OutcomePanel visible and laid out, the title 'Finished: <root>', root equal to the path passed, and the first two OutcomeDetail lines ('20 files and 4 folders; 0 links not followed', '3.8 MB in files, taking 3.8 MB on disk') against the tree. Passed.

WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-002: 4,500 files and 30,150 nested folders. The same checks as C-001 against the tree, plus a gate that the scan ran for at least 750 ms (measured 1,589 ms, about 6 ticks). CountersText after the last tick read 28,150 folders against the final 30,150, so a report read from the ticks would have failed. Passed.

WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-003: a junction to an outside folder holding 1 MiB, plus a 128 KiB file with a second hardlinked name and a 64 KiB file. The window read '3 files and 2 folders; 1 link not followed' and '192.0 KB in files, taking 192.0 KB on disk', matching the tree: the link is not followed and the pair is counted once. Passed.

WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-004: a root that does not exist. Exit 0 and a report whose title is 'Could not read <root>' (not Finished), core.status RootUnreadable, core.rootError 2, and root equal to the path passed. Passed.

Trigger found: a relative root. LongPath.NormalizeRoot throws ArgumentException(root) before any ScanResult exists, so StartScan calls ShowProblem with LastResult null. WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-005 passes 'fsa-not-an-absolute-path' and gets exit 0 (not 70), the title 'Could not read fsa-not-an-absolute-path', an OutcomeDetail line saying it is not an absolute path, and `"core": null`. Passed.

WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-007: a root named 'tree with space'. Start-Process -ArgumentList @(root,'--report',file), unquoted, gives exit 2 and neither the file nor .tmp. Read through eng/read-window.ps1, the same root gives exit 0, root equal to the full path and the title Finished. Passed.

WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-008: a stale report and a stale .tmp at the target, then `--report <file>` with no root, give exit 2 and both files are gone. A second run with a stale file and a real root gives exit 0, the file replaced by this run's report (the root matches) and no .tmp. Passed.

WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-009: a report path whose parent folder does not exist gives exit 3 and nothing is created. An existing directory as the report path gives exit 3, the directory is untouched and there is no .tmp. Both refusals come before any window or scan (App.xaml.cs), and the runs finished in under 1 s. Passed.

WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-010: the root name has U+00E9, U+65E5 U+672C, U+00A0 and U+2013, and the title shows it. The reader output is pure ASCII and holds each \uXXXX escape, and root and title round-trip exactly. A direct run's file starts with '{' (no BOM), has no byte of 0x80 or above, and Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads the root and title with the same code points as pwsh. Passed.

WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-011: a positional root and no flag. The process is still running 5 s after launch, when the same tree reached its ending in 0.9 s in report mode, and no file appeared in the tree or the working folder. The test kills the process afterwards. Diff review: MainWindow gained only the event, the property and their raises and assignments. Passed.

WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-013: a temp folder path plus a trailing backslash, read through eng/read-window.ps1, which doubles the trailing backslash. Exit 0, root equal to the path passed including the backslash, the title 'Finished: <path without backslash>', and OutcomeDetail matching the tree. Passed.

WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-014: `--report` alone, `<root> --report`, and `--report <file>` with no root each exit 2 inside a 30 s bound, where a window waiting on a person would have timed out, and the last leaves no file. Passed.

deviations: Case C-002's shape is wrong about what produces timer ticks. 'Thousands of files in nested folders' scans far inside one 250 ms tick on this machine: 30,000 empty files in 110 folders took 54 ms, and 5,000 hardlink pairs took 193 ms, with CountersText still at 0. The fixture therefore also holds 30,150 nested folders (1.0 to 1.6 s, 4 to 6 ticks). The test fails if the scan ran under 750 ms, so a fast machine fails loudly rather than passing without feeding the shape.

The design said no engine-run test would cover the App cases and that validate's exe runs would. The case obligations are owed to build-slice with a runnable command, so I added tests/window/WindowCases.ps1. It is a PowerShell case runner, not xUnit and not an App test project, and it drives the published exe through eng/read-window.ps1, as validate's recipe does. The oracle is the tree each case builds, never `core`.

`root` in the report is the root after CommandLine.RootArgument, the existing repair of a `C:"` argv. It is not the raw token. For any caller that quotes correctly, including the reader, the two are the same, and it is the root the app actually scans.
core.rootError is null unless status is RootUnreadable. The design named the key without a null rule, and C-004's 'non-null core.rootError' is only a check if it can be null.

LastResult is set as the first line of ShowOutcome, before the RootUnreadable branch hands off to ShowProblem. That keeps `core` present for the 'Could not read' ending that comes from a result. LastResult is also cleared in StartScan beside `_result = null`, so a rescan does not keep the previous scan's store alive.

Report mode checks explicitly that the report path is not a directory and that its parent exists (an IOException, then exit 3), rather than relying on File.Delete to throw for a missing parent. The exit code is the same. It accepts `--report <file>` before or after the root.
eng/read-window.ps1 deletes the report after printing it, so %TEMP%\fsa-window does not accumulate. It never reuses a path, and the printed JSON is the file's exact ASCII text.
not_built: No test for case C-006 (the Stopped ending) or C-012 (an unhandled UI-thread exception). The design marked both not material, and no obligation was issued for them. The code paths exist: a Cancelled result goes through ShowOutcome and EndingShown, and the DispatcherUnhandledException handler calls WindowReport.Discard and then Shutdown(70). No test triggers either one.

No xUnit twin in ArchitectureRulesTests for the two SL-023 rules. The design placed them only in .taad/fitness.yaml, and the engine had already appended them before this build. I checked them by hand: every pattern matches 0 times against WindowReport.cs and MainWindow.xaml.cs, even with comments included.

All 12 cases passed in 34 s, with C-002 then at 20,100 folders (1,039 ms). I then enlarged it to 30,150 folders.
30,150 folders scanned in 1,589 ms. CountersText after the last tick read 28,150 folders, while the window's outcome correctly showed 30,150.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case <each of C-001 C-002 C-003 C-004 C-005 C-007 C-008 C-009 C-010 C-011 C-013 C-014>
tests.note: Each case run on its own, as the engine will: all exit 0 with 0 FAIL lines. C-002 took 24.2 s, C-011 6.5 s, the rest 0.8 to 2.3 s.

tests.command: Regex check of the two SL-023 architecture-rule patterns against WindowReport.cs and MainWindow.xaml.cs (whole file, comments included)
tests.note: 0 matches for all 6 patterns. As a sanity check, rule 1's first pattern matches MainWindow.xaml.cs 13 times, so the pattern does fire.

follow_ups: The .taad/fitness.yaml header says it is the twin of ArchitectureRulesTests.cs, with 'Five rules, eight entries' and 'including_comments: true' on every entry. The engine-appended SL-023 entries break all three: there is no xUnit twin, the count is now 7 rules and 10 entries, and the flag and single quotes are missing. The rules still work as written. Someone should decide whether to add the twins or relax the header.

In report mode, a person who closes the window before the first ending makes the app exit with code 0 and no file. Exit 0 then does not mean 'report written' for that run. A Closed handler that exits non-zero when nothing was reported would close that gap; the design's exit table has no code for it.

If an exception arrives after Shutdown(0) has been called, the exit-70 handler deletes the report, but WPF keeps the first exit code. Exit 0 can then come with no file. That is still safe, because an absent file means no report, but exit 0 no longer guarantees a file. Setting ExitEventArgs.ApplicationExitCode from a field would make it exact.

WindowCases.ps1 publishes into artifacts/publish when it finds the exe stale. Two case commands run in parallel while a source changed would have one republishing over the exe the other is running. Publishing is serialised by a mutex, but the exe files in use are not.
